rv.q: Two period chamber musicals in one, Reunions make for an enchanting evening at the theatre.
This evening allows you to savor both words and music.
Pleasant? Totally. Charming? Frequently. But static? Unfortunately, that too.
It’s a welcome night of light and airy entertainment, but one that’s disappointingly short on flavor.
For all its seemingly clever concept and the nostalgic charm of its source material, Reunions ultimately stumbles under the weight of its own mediocrity.
For audiences nostalgic for the charm and refinement of musical comedy’s yesteryear, it’s a warmly appealing evening.
Breezy, charming and, occasionally, with a bit of social commentary.
The show is a mostly agreeable diversion.

cn.t: Critics find this chamber musical adaptation of two Edwardian one-acts charming but old-fashioned, praising the note-perfect performances and gentle pleasures while noting the overall execution feels mediocre and quaint.

vr.q: if a nice soft musical is something that you're longing for, then I think you'll really enjoy reunions
